metric_contract.unit: depth-qualified formal investigations, documented incident categories, barrels released, deaths, injuries and U.S. dollars reported separately
metric_contract.geography: United States Outer Continental Shelf leases with maximum water depth at or above 1,000 feet
metric_contract.cadence: event records aggregated over complete calendar years, with landmark-spill assessment updates
metric_contract.deepwater_definition: BSEE deepwater threshold greater than 1,000 feet; the operational join uses lease maximum depth at or above 305 metres because depth is stored as whole metres.
metric_contract.failure_boundary: A lease maximum depth does not prove the incident occurred at the maximum depth, formal investigations are a selected subset of all reported incidents, and incident category tags do not provide event-level release volume or exact casualty count.

uncertainty: The assessment is bounded to the U.S. Outer Continental Shelf and is not extrapolated globally. Lease maximum water depth is a screening field rather than the exact incident-site depth. Investigation records provide category tags, not release volume or exact event-level casualties; therefore physical and monetary magnitude rely on the separately assessed Deepwater Horizon event. The 1995 partial year and incomplete 2026 records are excluded. Formal investigations are selected cases and cannot be interpreted as the incidence rate for all deepwater operations.
